correctness.rationale: Each conditional cavity quadrature is a centered Gaussian with exact linear covariance ODE. Reduction to a two-mode affine PDMP gives stationary flux equations and explicit beta/gamma densities normalized to the known pump occupancy. Tail exponents and coefficients follow by integrating the endpoint densities, the critical Laplace principle, and Gaussian-mixture regular-variation integration. Photon moment thresholds follow by Wick factorization with bounded orthogonal quadrature. The Markov-cycle Lyapunov argument proves stationarity exactly below the strict boundary. Actual packaged verify.py checks mode masses, generator residual, moment integrals, and Gaussian-mixture tail limits; numerical checks alone are not the proof.

originality.rationale: The precise theorem is the optical observable-level conjunction: a telegraph-pump stationary region extending above the prescribed-pump threshold, three sharply distinguished intracavity homodyne logarithmic/regularly varying tails with an explicit leading Pareto coefficient, and separate finite mean photon versus second factorial photon thresholds. It is not asserted that Markov switching density formulas or OU moment-instability principles are themselves new. Full available motivating text and two generic methodological sources, related abstract-level physical papers, search records, and accessible earlier claims were compared for statement-level coverage; none inspected established all these optical observables. An uninspected alternate optical literature derivation remains possible.
residual_risks: Dichotomous switching density techniques predate this work. An explicit telegraph-pumped optical homodyne specialization could be present in unindexed or inaccessible materials, including older pump-fluctuation quantum-optics literature.
The optical source article gives covariance evolution; the theorem applies a Markov modulation not considered there.
Only abstract-level comparison was possible for the alternative pump-fluctuation paper and some nonlinear-oscillator papers; this does not prove full-text noncoverage.

value.rationale: The sharp optical observable-level trichotomy is a motivated failure mode and diagnostic for stochastic squeezing. It distinguishes a normalizable stationary density operator from finite mean energy and finite photon-pair factorial moment and provides the exact power tail coefficient for an intracavity homodyne measurement. The finite-energy and higher-moment boundaries are distinct from the prescribed-pump deterministic threshold; this is a structurally meaningful phase diagram, not an arbitrary numerical slice or unsupported gain claim.
